faq.q: What is the origin of Aasimah?
faq.a: Aasimah is associated with Arabic. Variant romanization of aasima.
Yes — the underlying form عاصمة is Arabic.
Aasimah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aasimah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. root ع ص م occurs in the Qur'an; عاصمة is a normal Arabic feminine form

faq.q: What does Aasimah mean in Urdu?

faq.q: What does Aasimah mean in Persian?
faq.a: No verified Persian form was established for Aasimah.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aasimah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aasimah, aasimah, asimah. Script forms are عاصمة, عاصمه, عاصمہ, आसिमा.

faq.q: Is Aasimah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
